evidence.rootCause: recordedStop rebuilds each earlier break from the declaration the recorded return listed (decl.get(b.eventId), checked by inputHash; startedAt = utcTimestamp(i.startedAt) of that declaration), never from a newer report of the same episode. A restatement with the start time is therefore never read on this path. It also becomes a new separate break that ends before an applied return, which the pre-existing episode rules ask as one period on every review (true on all runtimes, but only the candidate instructs it). The named report of the trip stays on the record, so each later review re-runs returnAfterPause -> recordedStop -> stopOf -> ownReturnOf, and r.material && !by.sport.STRENGTH asks again. staleReturn reaches the same branch through recordedStop(onlyOwnReturn), and its F04 decision replaces I6's confirmation question.
evidence.notDetectedBy: T25 covers only the separate-breaks path. No test exercises F04 inside recordedStop or staleReturn. No harness property flags a persistent ASK. No corpus case has a late first-day lift after an own return, or a correction that removes strength's re-entry week, so the differential and the decomposition could not see it.

A later candidate must let every re-read path read the answer: an earlier break's start time restated after an applied return read it (for example, recordedStop reading the newest readable report of each listed episode and asking only when facts other than the start time changed), or the question must not be raised where its answer cannot be read.
